/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 15 October 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2545 (-122)
Baltic Capesize Index: 3322 (-308)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2356 (-53)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1856 (11)
Baltic Handysize Index: 1007 (4)
CAPESIZE
Halfway through the week, the market continued to face downward pressure, with losses extending across both basins. The BCI 182 5TC fell by a further $2,792 to $30,128, while the C5 and C3 routes dropped by $0.800 to $11.250 and $1.060 to $30.550, respectively. In the Pacific, sentiment remained weak with relatively limited level of activity. One C5 miner was active alongside a handful of operators and a few tender cargoes, but this proved insufficient to halt the downward trend. Bids started around $11.00, while offers quickly moved below the previous done level of $12.10 and into the upper $11s. The market eventually saw $11.25 concluded on a couple of occasions, underlining the continued erosion in rates. The Atlantic remained very lacklustre, with limited activity and weakening sentiment adding to the pressure. Rates from South Brazil and West Africa to China continued to slide, with the C3 losing another dollar. A fixture at $30.50 for mid-November dates reflected the softer conditions. With both basins continuing to lose ground and little evidence of improving demand, the market remains firmly on the defensive as the week progresses.
PANAMAX
The Atlantic market endured another day of negative sentiment, while in the Pacific some market participants suggested a rate ceiling may have been reached, resulting in the P5TC declining by $480 to $21,200. Brokers reported that the North Continent is becoming increasingly long on tonnage, with trans-Atlantic demand insufficient to absorb the growing supply. Market sources noted that bids are either falling or disappearing altogether, with owners not under pressure to fix ahead of the weekend expected to step back and wait for fresh demand to emerge. Fronthaul business is following a similar trend, as mounting tonnage availability continues to weigh on rates, while grain demand remains limited and the US Gulf has failed to generate the level of activity many had anticipated. Conditions in the South Atlantic are also said to be deteriorating, with owners repeatedly revising expectations lower amid a growing ballaster list, subdued bidding interest and increasing pressure on both fronthaul and trans-Atlantic returns. In the Pacific, market fundamentals are said to remain relatively resilient, with increased activity from the North Pacific helping to support sentiment. However, in contrast to recent days, demand from East Coast Australia has reportedly eased, as charterers take a step back to reassess their forward requirements and schedules. The Flag Hope (93,242 2011) open Jintang 16/17 October fixed a trip with coal via East Coast Australia to Singapore-Japan range in the region of $20,150-$21,000 to NYK. The Myrsini (82,117 2010) Cai Lan 21/25 October was reported to have fixed, but no other information was heard.
SUPRAMAX
Another positive index today with the 11TC average up $139 to $23,466. The US Gulf demand seemed to shrink with plentiful tonnage the fronthaul offers were reduced, whilst transatlantic numbers somehow seemed to remain steady for the timebeing. In the south activity centred around fronthaul trades and rates appear to be holding, despite talk of softer levels yesterday. The Continent saw some old scrap fixtures emerge at very strong levels, but they were concluded at the end of last week, and sources now suggest that was the peak with rates still good but slightly below reports. The Mediterranean has seen more activity and rates improving on certain trades, but not across the board. The Amfitriti (58,814 2010) went on subjects to Pangaea basis delivery Egyptian Med for a trip Baltimore with salt at $12,500 and the Angele N (55,804 2010) failed on subjects with WBC basis delivery Garrucha for a trip Conakry with gypsum at $18,000, but has apparently refixed with XO for another trip West Africa, but there were no further details. Asia continues to tick along with rates slowly rising day-by-day, with NoPac delivering firm levels and certain backhauls concluded at impressive numbers. South East Asia has also been active and with rates to China also up now, following the Indonesia/India improvements.
HANDYSIZE
A mixed day with the HS7TC average up $75 to $18,131. East coast South America really appeared to be pushing as a tight tonnage supply took hold, whilst the US Gulf was the opposite with a softer undertone due to plentiful supply. Across the basin the Continent and Mediterranean remained balanced with little movement evident. In Asia the North Pacific felt stronger and offers were slightly higher, whilst South East Asia remained flat.

Atlantic
A 38,000-dwt was said to be on subjects from Santos to the Mediterranean at $29,500, and later in the day we heard a 39,000-dwt had fixed from EC South America to the Continent at $32,000, but further details were lacking on both trades. The Gdynia (37,933 2012) was reported fixed to Bunge from the US Gulf to Puerto Cortes at $16,500 and the Yasa Tulip (40,238 2023) went on subjects to Pacnav for an intercaribs to EC Mexico trip at $17,500.

Asia
The Rahma (35,829 2011) Karachi end October fixed a trip US West Coast with steels in the low $15,000’s, whilst the Golf (37,856 2011) open EC India apparently failed for a steels trip to the Continent at $14,500. The Kinling (37,440 2022) which sailed Chittagong 7 Oct fixed via EC India to South China with granite at around $11,000, although it may have fixed a while ago, and the Agia Filothei (38,221 2012) spot Gangavaram was reported at around $18,000 for a trip to Africa, but there were no further details.

Market Fundamentals
HRB Steel Prices
In the two weeks to 14 October, the US hot rolled band (HRB) price rose $17/t to $1,310/t, the highest since June 2022, World Steel Dynamics data show. In contrast, the Chinese and Western European HRB price eased $2/t and $7/t to a respective $422/t and $835/t.

Trading Commentary
Cape
Cape remained sharply weaker, with heavy activity across Nov, Q1 and Cal 27, although the front months recovered from afternoon lows.
